# northflank_addon (Resource)

Manages a Northflank addon: a managed database, cache or message queue such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis or RabbitMQ.

Creating an addon waits until it is running, so that `secrets` and `connection_details` are usable by whatever depends on it. Destroying it waits until it is gone.

**Destroying this resource deletes the addon and its data**, and so does changing `name`, `type`, `project_id` or `database_name`. Consider `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`. Credentials are stored in Terraform state; treat the state file as a secret.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "northflank_project" "app" {
  name   = "My Application"
  region = "europe-west"
}

# A two-replica PostgreSQL 16 database. Creating it waits until it is running.
resource "northflank_addon" "db" {
  project_id      = northflank_project.app.id
  name            = "Main DB"
  type            = "postgresql"
  version         = "16"
  deployment_plan = "nf-compute-20"
  replicas        = 2
  storage_size    = 8192
  tls_enabled     = true
  database_name   = "app"

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

# Hand the connection string to a service. Which keys connection_details has
# depends on the addon type, and the one below is illustrative: after the first
# apply, `terraform console` and `nonsensitive(keys(northflank_addon.db.connection_details))`
# show the real ones. Alternatively, link the addon to a secret group in the
# Northflank dashboard.
resource "northflank_deployment_service" "api" {
  project_id      = northflank_project.app.id
  name            = "API"
  deployment_plan = "nf-compute-20"

  deployment = {
    external_image = {
      image_path = "ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4"
    }
  }

  runtime_environment = {
    DATABASE_URL = northflank_addon.db.connection_details["POSTGRES_URI"]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `deployment_plan` (String) ID of the compute plan each replica uses, such as `nf-compute-20`.
- `name` (String) Name of the addon, 3 to 39 characters. Changing this forces a new addon, since Northflank derives the `id` from it and cannot rename one.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the addon belongs to. Changing this forces a new addon.
- `storage_size` (Number) Storage per replica, in megabytes, such as `4096`. Changes are applied in place; Northflank may refuse to shrink storage.
- `type` (String) Kind of addon, such as `postgresql`, `mysql`, `mongodb`, `redis`, `rabbitmq` or `minio`. The Northflank API lists the types available to a team at `GET /v1/addon-types`. Changing this forces a new addon.
- `version` (String) Version to run, such as `16.4.0`, a prefix of one such as `16`, or `latest` for the newest available at creation. Raising it upgrades the addon in place; Northflank may refuse to downgrade. `running_version` shows the exact version, and a newer release is not applied until `version` asks for it.

### Optional

- `database_name` (String) Name of the database to create, for types that support choosing it. Can only be set at creation, so changing it forces a new addon. The API does not report it back.
- `description` (String) Short description of the addon, up to 200 characters. Removing it from configuration keeps the current value.
- `external_access` (Boolean) Make the addon reachable from the internet, over TLS. Cannot be combined with `vpc_accessible`. Defaults to `false`.
- `replicas` (Number) Number of replicas to run. Defaults to `1`.
- `storage_class` (String) Storage class, such as `nvme`. Only configurable on accounts with the feature enabled; Northflank picks its default otherwise.
- `tags` (Set of String) Previously defined Northflank tags to attach to the addon.
- `tls_enabled` (Boolean) Serve connections over TLS, for types that support it. Defaults to `false`.
- `vpc_accessible` (Boolean) Expose the addon on the cluster's private (VPC) load balancer. Cannot be combined with `external_access`. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `app_id` (String) Full identifier Northflank uses for the addon.
- `connection_details` (Map of String, Sensitive) Connection details such as hosts, ports and connection strings, keyed as Northflank names them for the addon type.
- `created_at` (String) Creation time, in RFC 3339 format.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the addon, derived by Northflank from `name`.
- `region` (String) Region the addon is deployed in.
- `running_version` (String) Version the addon actually runs.
- `secrets` (Map of String, Sensitive) Secrets for connecting, such as `username` and `password`. Which keys exist depends on the addon type.
- `status` (String) State of the addon, such as `running`, `paused` or `upgrading`.
- `uid` (String) Permanent identifier of the addon. Unlike `id`, it never changes and is never reused.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Addons are imported as <project_id>/<addon_id>. database_name is not
# reported by the API, so it is taken from configuration afterwards.
terraform import northflank_addon.db my-application/main-db
```
